findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses raw String for status and separate bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of typed enums or typestates. Illegal states are constructable: status can be 'sent' while is_sent is false, or both booleans can be true simultaneously, or status can be an arbitrary string with no domain constraint.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct PacketWorkflow with contradictory state (e.g., status='new', is_sent=true), making the domain invariant invisible to the compiler and requiring runtime checks everywhere the struct is consumed.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed enum (e.g., PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }). Replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with a typestate enum or derive them from PacketStatus. Provide a fallible constructor that rejects invalid transitions. Remove pub fields; use methods or a builder.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. Any string, empty string, or malformed ID is accepted with no validation at the boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or empty IDs silently pass through the system. No compile-time distinction between a valid packet ID and a garbage string. Every consumer must re-validate.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype struct PacketId(String) with a private field and a fallible constructor (e.g., fn new(s: String) -> Result<PacketId, InvalidIdError>) that rejects empty/invalid IDs. Use PacketId in PacketWorkflow.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are two independent flags that encode a state machine. This allows the four boolean combinations (00, 01, 10, 11) when the domain likely permits fewer valid transitions.
findings.failure_mode: The (validated=true, sent=false) state contradicts the likely domain expectation that sent packets are also validated. The (validated=false, sent=true) state represents an invalid transition (sent without validation). Both true is ambiguous.
findings.fix: Collapse into a single typestate enum, e.g., enum PacketState { New, Validated, Sent }. Derive sent_at_epoch_ms as part of the Sent transition. This makes illegal state combinations unconstructable at compile time.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> has no domain constraint on valid epoch values. The field accepts any u64 including zero or nonsensical epochs, and there is no constructor enforcing that sent_at_epoch_ms is only Some when status indicates sent.
findings.failure_mode: A PacketWorkflow can have sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) or Some(1) while is_sent=false, representing a nonsensical timestamp. Zero epoch may also be confused with None by consumers.
findings.fix: Tie sent_at_epoch_ms to the typestate: remove it as a separate field and instead include the timestamp in the Sent variant of the typestate enum (e.g., PacketState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }). Remove Option wrapper entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes PacketWorkflow by value and mutates it in place, but the struct has no invariants to enforce. The function blindly overwrites status and sets is_sent without checking prior state or enforcing transition rules.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called on any PacketWorkflow regardless of its current state (e.g., marking an already-sent packet again, or marking an unvalidated packet as sent). No preconditions are checked.
findings.fix: With the typestate enum, mark_sent becomes a method or pure function on the typestate that only accepts the pre-sent state and returns the post-sent state. e.g., fn mark_sent(state: PacketState, now_ms: u64) -> Result<PacketState, InvalidTransitionError>. The domain invariant is enforced by the type system.

findings.problem: All fields of PacketWorkflow are pub, allowing any caller to directly mutate status, is_validated, and is_sent without going through domain methods. This bypasses any transition logic.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set item.status = "sent" directly without calling mark_sent, without setting is_sent, and without recording sent_at_epoch_ms, leaving the struct in an inconsistent state.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide only domain methods for state transitions (e.g., validate(), mark_sent()). Alternatively, use an enum-based typestate where transitions are the only way to change state.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() which always allocates a new String for 'sent'. Combined with pub id: String and pub status: String, the struct requires heap allocation for every field and accepts unbounded string lengths.
findings.failure_mode: Memory usage is unbounded and unpredictable. A malicious caller can construct PacketWorkflow with extremely long id or status strings. The to_string() in mark_sent always allocates even when the new value equals the current one.
findings.fix: Replace status with an enum (zero allocation). Use a newtype for id with a constructor that enforces max length. If id must remain heap-allocated, consider bounded String or OsString. mark_sent should take the state by value and return a new state without intermediate allocation.

residual_risk: The domain model is fundamentally broken: illegal states are representable, bool flags encode a state machine unsafely, fields are publicly mutable, and mark_sent has no precondition checks. A rework using newtypes, a sealed typestate enum, and private fields with typed transition methods is required before any further development. Static review only; no commands were run.
